@servers.hub.colName.description: Column heading in the servers hub: the server''s own name. One or two words; the column is narrow.

@servers.hub.colType.description: Column heading in the servers hub for which protocol a server speaks (SFTP, WebDAV, SMB). One word.

@servers.hub.colAddress.description: Column heading in the servers hub for where the server lives: a hostname, an IP address, or a web address. One word.

@servers.hub.colStatus.description: Column heading in the servers hub for how the server is doing right now. One word.

@servers.hub.colLastUsed.description: Column heading in the servers hub for when the user last connected to the server. Two words at most.

@servers.hub.addServer.description: The last row of the servers hub, which opens the form for typing a new server. VERB phrase, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means "this opens something"; keep it.

@servers.hub.status.connected.description: Status of a server the app is talking to right now. One word, ADJECTIVE.

@servers.hub.status.saved.description: Status of a server the user has saved but isn''t connected to. Nothing is wrong; it''s simply idle. One word, ADJECTIVE.

@servers.hub.status.foundNearby.description: Status of a server Cmdr can see on the local network right now, whether or not the user saved it. Two words.

@servers.hub.status.signedOut.description: Status of a saved server whose session ended because a password is what''s missing. ❗ NOT a rejection and not a fault: the user simply has to sign in again.

servers.hub.status.waitingForKey: Waiting for you to check the key

@servers.hub.status.waitingForKey.description: Status of an SSH server whose identity key the user hasn''t approved yet. "The key" is the server''s SSH host key, a fingerprint a person compares before trusting the server. Address the user directly.

@servers.hub.neverUsed.description: Shown in the servers hub''s "Last used" column for a server the user has never connected to. One word.

@servers.hub.discoveryOff.description: One line in the servers hub, in place of the list of servers found nearby, when the user has turned local network discovery off in Settings. Saved servers still work and are still listed; this line is only about the nearby ones.

@servers.hub.discoveryOffLink.description: Link beside the discovery-off line; it opens Settings at the switch that turns local network discovery back on. VERB phrase, imperative. "Settings" is the app''s own Settings window; use the word your language''s macOS uses for it.

@servers.hub.emptyTitle.description: Heading of the empty state in the servers hub, when the user has saved none and Cmdr found none nearby. Short and neutral.

servers.hub.emptyMessage: Add one below, or turn on a Mac or NAS on your network and Cmdr will find it.

@servers.hub.emptyMessage.description: One line under the empty-state heading in the servers hub. "NAS" is a network storage box; keep the abbreviation if your language uses it, otherwise say the equivalent. "below" points at the "Add server…" row at the bottom of the list.

@servers.hub.rowCount.description: The count in the status bar under the servers hub. Counts saved servers and nearby ones together, and excludes the "Add server…" row.

placeholders.count: the number, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.countText: the number as the user''s locale writes it, like "1,024"

@servers.paneState.connecting.description: Heading of the pane view shown while Cmdr opens a connection to a server. {name} is the server''s display name. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).

servers.paneState.connectingHint: This can take a few seconds.

@servers.paneState.connectingHint.description: One line under the connecting heading, setting the expectation that a server handshake is not instant. Reassurance, not an instruction.

@servers.paneState.cancel.description: Button that calls off a connection Cmdr is in the middle of opening. VERB, imperative.

@servers.paneState.tryAgain.description: Button that starts the same connection over after it was refused. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.paneState.disconnect.description: Button that drops the server''s session and leaves the pane. VERB, imperative. A server has nothing to unplug, so it says Disconnect rather than Eject.

@servers.refusal.authenticationRejected.description: Shown in the pane when the server refused the credential Cmdr offered. Factual, not accusing: the password may have changed on the server side.

placeholders.username: the account name on the server, like "ada"

servers.refusal.needsCredentials: This server asks for a password.

@servers.refusal.needsCredentials.description: Shown in the pane when the server wants a credential and Cmdr has none stored. ❗ NOT a rejection: nothing was ever offered, so don''t word it as a wrong password.

servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported: This server uses a sign-in method Cmdr doesn''t support yet.

@servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported.description: Shown in the pane when the server challenged with an authentication scheme Cmdr doesn''t speak. The secret was never sent, so nothing about it is known to be wrong. ❌ Don''t name the scheme: it means nothing to the reader.

servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted: macOS doesn''t trust this server''s certificate. Add it in Keychain Access, then try again.

@servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted.description: Shown in the pane when a WebDAV server''s TLS certificate isn''t trusted by the operating system. "Keychain Access" is the macOS app name, which the OS ships translated; use the name your language''s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer: Nothing at this address answers WebDAV.

@servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer.description: Shown in the pane when the address answers as a web server but doesn''t speak WebDAV. "WebDAV" is a protocol name; don''t translate it.

servers.refusal.invalidUrl: That doesn''t look like a server address.

@servers.refusal.invalidUrl.description: Shown in the pane when the saved address isn''t a usable web address at all.

@servers.refusal.timedOut.description: Shown in the pane when the server didn''t finish the handshake inside Cmdr''s budget.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.refusal.unreachable.description: Shown in the pane when there was no route to the server at all: it''s off, the name doesn''t resolve, or the network is down. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.refusal.hostKeyUntrusted.description: Shown in the pane when an SSH server presents a host key this Mac hasn''t approved. "Key" is the server''s SSH host key, the fingerprint a person checks before trusting the server.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked: {host}''s key is marked as compromised in your SSH settings on this Mac. Cmdr won''t connect to it.

@servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked.description: Shown in the pane when the server''s SSH host key is listed as revoked in the user''s own known_hosts file. This one is deliberately final: there is no button that can safely undo it. "SSH" is a protocol name; don''t translate it.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.sheet.addTitle.description: Title of the sheet where the user types a new server. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.signInTitle.description: Title of the sheet when a server is asking for a credential. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.editTitle.description: Title of the sheet when the user is changing a server they already saved. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.connect.description: The sheet's main button in add mode: it dials the server the user typed. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.signIn.description: The sheet's main button when a server is asking for a credential. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.save.description: The sheet's main button when the user is editing a saved server. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.cancel.description: The sheet's secondary button: it closes without connecting or saving. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.connecting.description: Replaces the main buttons label while the sheet is waiting for the server. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).

@servers.sheet.protocolLegend.description: Accessible name of the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV picker in the add form. Screen readers only; not visible. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.protocolSmb.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.protocolSftp.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.protocolWebdav.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.address.description: Label of the field where the user types where the server lives. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.addressPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the address field. A short example hostname; leave it as-is or use an equally short one.

servers.sheet.addressHelp: A hostname, an address you copied, or a whole ssh line. Cmdr picks the protocol.

@servers.sheet.addressHelp.description: One line under the address field, telling the user they can paste whatever they have. “Cmdr” is the product name; “ssh” is a command name, keep it lowercase and untranslated.

@servers.sheet.username.description: Label of the account field. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.password.description: Label of the password field. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.passphrase.description: Label of the field for the passphrase that unlocks an SSH key FILE, which is not the account's password. Two words.

@servers.sheet.remember.description: Checkbox that stores the password in the macOS Keychain. “Keychain” is the macOS feature name, which the OS ships translated; use the name your language's macOS uses.

@servers.sheet.connectionModeLegend.description: Accessible name of the guest-or-account choice for a share that allows both. Screen readers only; not visible.

@servers.sheet.connectAsGuest.description: One option: open the share without an account, which some servers allow. VERB phrase, imperative.

servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials: Sign in with a username and password

@servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials.description: The other option: open the share as a named account. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.advanced.description: A collapsed section holding the settings most people never change. One word, ADJECTIVE.

servers.sheet.name: Name

@servers.sheet.name.description: Label of the field for what to call this server in the app. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.remoteFolder.description: Label of the field for which folder ON THE SERVER to open at. Two words.

@servers.sheet.keyFile.description: Label of the field for the SSH private key file to sign in with. “Key” is an SSH key. Two words.

@servers.sheet.browse.description: Button beside the key-file field; it opens the system file picker. VERB, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means “this opens something”; keep it.

@servers.sheet.useAgent.description: Checkbox letting Cmdr ask the running ssh-agent for a key. “ssh-agent” is a program name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.autoReconnect.description: Checkbox letting Cmdr redial this server on its own when the connection drops. VERB phrase, imperative.

servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret: Reconnecting on its own needs a remembered password. Turn on “Remember in Keychain” and sign in once.

@servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret.description: Shown in the edit sheet when “Reconnect automatically” is on but nothing is stored, so it can never actually run. Says what to do about it.

@servers.sheet.tryNextcloudAddress.description: Button offered when a web address answers but doesn't speak WebDAV. It appends the path Nextcloud and ownCloud keep their files under. “Nextcloud” is a product name; keep it as-is. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.hostKey.firstContactTitle.description: Heading of the step where the user approves a servers SSH identity key the first time. Routine, not alarming.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like “nas.local”

servers.hostKey.firstContactBody: Check the fingerprint below against the one the server''s owner gave you, then trust it.

@servers.hostKey.firstContactBody.description: One line under that heading. “Fingerprint” is the short string that identifies an SSH key; a person compares it character by character.

@servers.hostKey.changedTitle.description: Heading of the same step when the server presents a DIFFERENT key than the one already trusted. This one is serious: it can mean someone is in the middle.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like “nas.local”

servers.hostKey.changedBody: This can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the fingerprint with the server''s owner before trusting it.

@servers.hostKey.changedBody.description: One line under the changed-key heading. Says both innocent and serious causes, and what to do first.

@servers.hostKey.changedDisclosure.description: A collapsed section holding the button that trusts a CHANGED key. Deliberately behind a click, so trusting one is never a reflex. First person: the user speaking.

@servers.hostKey.fingerprintLabel.description: Label above the SSH keys algorithm and fingerprint. Two words, NOUN phrase.

@servers.hostKey.trustAndConnect.description: Button that records a first-contact key and carries on connecting. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.hostKey.trustNewKey.description: Button that records a CHANGED key, behind the disclosure. VERB phrase, imperative.
